lines.text: The nineteen-oh-four Olympic marathon in St. Louis was so wildly disastrous, it felt like a slapstick comedy film.
Runners raced twenty-five miles through ninety-degree heat over dusty unpaved roads choked with car exhaust.
The race organizers intentionally provided only one single water station to test human dehydration limits.
One runner hitched a ride in an automobile for eleven miles, crossed the finish line, and almost took the gold medal.
Another runner ate rotten apples from an orchard, developed agonizing stomach cramps, and took an hour nap by the road.
The actual winner was repeatedly injected with rat poison strychnine and raw egg whites as a stimulant, hallucinating across the finish line.
It remains the most bizarre and chaotic athletic event ever staged in Olympic history.
